name: e.l.f. Beauty, Inc.

profile.description: e.l.f. Beauty, Inc. is a multi-brand beauty company offering cosmetics, skincare, and beauty tools at accessible price points. The portfolio includes e.l.f. Cosmetics, e.l.f. SKIN, Naturium, Well People, and rhode (acquired 2024). Headquartered in Oakland, California, e.l.f. is the #1 mass cosmetics brand in the US by market share.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): e.l.f. executed multiple transformative moves over the past 5 years — acquiring Naturium (clean skincare, 2024), partnering with Hailey Bieber's rhode brand, and expanding from pure cosmetics into a multi-brand skincare and wellness platform [1]. FY2026 marked the 7th consecutive year of net sales and market share growth, with all five brands growing [1]. AI Deployment (1/2): Invested $4.2M in AI-powered skin analysis tools including the color e.l.f.nalysis diagnostic tool and AR/metaverse experiences, plus launched an Apple Vision Pro spatial computing experience led by Chief Digital Officer Ekta Chopra [3]. These are shipping but early-stage revenue contributors. Market Share (2/2): e.l.f. is the #1 mass cosmetics brand in the US, consistently gaining market share for 7 consecutive years, forcing premium competitors to respond to its price-value proposition [1][3]. Product Pipeline (1/2): rhode and Naturium continue rapid expansion, and international growth accelerates, but specific next-gen product launches with dates are not publicly disclosed [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): As a beauty brand, R&D intensity is moderate and not top-quartile for the personal products sector.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): e.l.f.'s purpose — 'standing with every eye, lip and face' — is specific, inclusive, and differentiated, connecting beauty accessibility to empowerment across demographics. CEO Tarang Amin has articulated this purpose consistently over his 12-year tenure, and it shapes product and pricing strategy [4]. The team is 74% women, 76% Gen Z/millennials, and 44% diverse, with a board that is 67% women [4]. Community Impact (1/2): First and only beauty company with six Fair Trade Certified manufacturing facilities; achieved FSC certification for 100% of packaging in FY2026 [4]. General corporate social responsibility but lacking distinctive dollar-amount philanthropic commitments. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor rating of 3.2/5 based on 254 reviews — below average. Reviews cite leadership changes impacting morale, political dynamics, and trust erosion, though some praise transparency and risk-taking culture [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): Net insider selling throughout 2025-2026. CEO Tarang Amin sold $3.9M in stock in July 2026, and earlier sales of 41,520 shares and 15,829 shares were for tax withholding on vested RSUs [5]. No discretionary insider purchases identified.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. e.l.f. delivered FY2026 net sales of $1.64B (up 25% YoY), marking the 7th consecutive year of revenue growth, but profitability collapsed due to Trump tariff exposure on China-sourced manufacturing — net income fell 77% to $26.3M and profit margin compressed to 1.61% [1][2]. The 5-year revenue CAGR of 42.1% is exceptional, reflecting the company's rapid scaling from $283M in FY2021 [2]. However, D/E of 81% exceeds the 70% target, ROE plummeted to 2.78% from double digits in FY2025, and the Forward PEG of 2.12 signals growth is priced at a premium [2]. Forward P/E of 22.53 is slightly above the 20 target. The tariff-driven earnings collapse is the dominant infrastructure headwind, masking an otherwise strong revenue growth engine.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): e.l.f.'s core business — manufacturing and selling physical cosmetics, skincare, and beauty tools — is inherently protected from AI disruption [3]. Beauty products require physical application, sensory evaluation, brand trust, and emotional/social connections that AI cannot replicate. Retail distribution through Target, Walmart, and Ulta creates physical-world moats. AI can enhance marketing personalization and product development but does not threaten the core revenue model. Some modest risk exists from AI-generated beauty content shifting marketing dynamics, but e.l.f.'s brand equity and price-value proposition remain defensible [3]. AI Opportunity (0/1): While e.l.f. invested $4.2M in AI-powered skin analysis and AR experiences, these are engagement tools rather than revenue-generating AI products. No quantifiable AI revenue contribution has been disclosed [3].

infinite_game.summary: e.l.f. Beauty demonstrates a genuine purpose in democratizing beauty access, and CEO Tarang Amin's 12-year tenure provides strategic consistency. The company showed courage in maintaining accessible pricing during inflation while competitors raised prices, and acquired rhode and Naturium to expand its mission. However, Glassdoor reviews (3.2/5) reveal cultural tensions — leadership changes impacted morale and trust, with some employees describing a reactive, political environment. The purpose is real but organizational trust has not been fully established.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Standing with every eye, lip and face' is a genuine, distinctive cause that connects beauty accessibility to inclusivity and empowerment [4]. CEO Amin references this purpose consistently, and strategic decisions (accessible pricing, diverse team composition, Fair Trade manufacturing) trace back to it. However, the cause has not been tested through a major existential crisis beyond the current tariff disruption, and it has not survived a leadership transition.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Mixed signals on organizational trust. Some Glassdoor reviews praise leadership as 'transparent, visionary, and empowering,' with teams encouraged to take risks and innovate [3]. However, the 3.2/5 overall rating and multiple reviews citing 'leadership changes significantly impacted morale, culture, and employee trust' suggest adequate but inconsistent trust [3]. The 74% women, 44% diverse workforce composition indicates inclusive culture, but execution on psychological safety appears uneven.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): e.l.f. explicitly benchmarks its product quality against premium beauty brands like Estee Lauder, MAC, and Charlotte Tilbury, using their strengths to demonstrate comparable quality at accessible price points [3]. This competitive framing focuses on learning from and matching rival quality rather than destroying competitors — a classic worthy rival mindset that drives continuous product improvement.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): e.l.f. evolved from a single cosmetics brand to a multi-brand beauty platform spanning cosmetics, skincare (Naturium), and celebrity-backed luxury-accessible brands (rhode) [1]. The expansion into skincare and the acquisition strategy represent genuine business model evolution. However, these are adjacent-market expansions rather than the kind of transformative, purpose-driven pivot that defines top scores.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): e.l.f. maintained its value pricing strategy during the 2022-2024 inflationary period while premium competitors raised prices, choosing long-term market share gains over short-term margin protection [1]. The Naturium acquisition and rhode partnership required significant capital commitment to expand the brand portfolio. However, the company's response to the tariff crisis — with net income falling 77% in FY2026 — has been more reactive (supply chain diversification) than proactively courageous [1].

investment_thesis: e.l.f. Beauty has built one of the most compelling consumer growth stories in the US market, delivering 7 consecutive years of net sales and market share growth with FY2026 revenue reaching $1.64B (up 25% YoY) [1]. The company is the #1 mass cosmetics brand in the US, and its multi-brand portfolio (e.l.f. Cosmetics, Naturium, rhode) provides diversified growth vectors across cosmetics, skincare, and celebrity beauty. The 5-year revenue CAGR of 42.1% demonstrates exceptional scaling ability. At $74.49 with a forward P/E of 22.53, the stock is reasonably valued relative to the revenue growth trajectory, and the company's price-value proposition resonates strongly with Gen Z and millennial consumers [2].
thesis_continued: The dominant risk is tariff-driven margin compression — FY2026 net income collapsed 77% to $26.3M as Trump tariffs on China-sourced manufacturing crushed profitability, compressing profit margin to 1.61% and ROE to 2.78% [1][2]. The company's heavy reliance on Chinese manufacturing (a competitive advantage pre-tariffs due to cost efficiency) has become a structural liability. Supply chain diversification is underway but will take 12-18 months to meaningfully reduce exposure. The trailing P/E of 169x reflects the earnings trough, and any delay in margin recovery could further pressure the stock, which is already down 30% over the past year [2]. Glassdoor concerns (3.2/5) about leadership culture add execution risk during a critical operational transition [3].
key_catalysts: Supply chain diversification away from China manufacturing expected to restore profit margins to mid-teens by FY2028, with management targeting tariff cost mitigation through sourcing shifts and selective price increases

rhode and Naturium brand expansion providing dual growth engines — both brands grew meaningfully in FY2026, and international expansion particularly in Europe offers a large untapped addressable market

Continued market share gains as the #1 mass cosmetics brand, with Gen Z brand loyalty and social media engagement driving organic growth as premium beauty brands lose share to value-oriented alternatives
key_risks: China tariff exposure remains the existential near-term risk — FY2026 net income fell 77% and any escalation in US-China trade tensions could further compress margins before supply chain diversification is complete

Valuation risk at 169x trailing P/E assumes a sharp earnings recovery that depends on successful tariff mitigation; if margins do not recover to pre-tariff levels of 12-15%, the stock faces significant multiple compression
CEO and leadership culture concerns (Glassdoor 3.2/5, net insider selling of $3.9M by CEO in July 2026) create execution risk during the most operationally complex period in the company's history
